trick: Biodiversity works at three levels — genetic, species and ecosystem — and a hotspot must satisfy two conditions at once: exceptional endemism AND serious threat. India has four hotspots: the Himalaya, the Western Ghats with Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland covering the Nicobars.

data.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of India's four biodiversity hotspots?
items: The Western Ghats and Sri Lanka
data.because: A hotspot needs exceptional endemism together with serious threat. The Thar has remarkable adaptations but does not meet the endemism threshold; India's four are the Himalaya, the Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Sundaland.

trick: In-situ means in the original place — national parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves. Ex-situ means out of it — zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, cryopreservation. The Latin does the work, so translate the prefix and every example sorts itself.

trick: EIA is done BEFORE a project is cleared, not after it is built — that timing is its whole purpose. Its steps run screening, scoping, impact prediction, public hearing, and finally the decision. The public hearing is the step most often omitted from an answer, and it is the one that gives affected people a voice.

trick: The dates run in a memorable order: Wildlife Protection 1972, Water 1974, Forest Conservation 1980, Air 1981, and the Environment (Protection) Act 1986 — the umbrella law passed in the wake of Bhopal. Articles 48A and 51A(g) put protection of the environment into the Constitution itself, as a directive and as a fundamental duty.

trick: Two tiers doing the same work at different levels: the Central Pollution Control Board advises the central government and coordinates, the State Boards grant consents and enforce on the ground. The CPCB was constituted in 1974 under the Water Act — the Act came first and created the Board, not the other way round.

trick: A hazard becomes a disaster only when it meets vulnerable people — an earthquake in an empty desert is not a disaster. Management runs in a cycle of four: prevention and mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. The NDMA was set up under the Disaster Management Act of 2005, after the 2004 tsunami.

trick: Learn the Brundtland definition word for word — development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs — and attach it to the report 'Our Common Future', 1987, chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland of Norway. trick: Two different problems in two different layers, and questions deliberately mix them. Ozone depletion is CFCs destroying ozone in the STRATOSPHERE, letting ultraviolet through, and it is addressed by the Montreal Protocol. Global warming is greenhouse gases trapping heat in the TROPOSPHERE, and it is addressed by Kyoto and Paris.
